removalExpectations.note: What must disappear when a parent choice changes, and what the evaluator actually does with a selection that is left behind.
removalExpectations.pruningSemantics: A stored selection whose decision becomes unavailable does not silently vanish: the evaluator raises an invalid unavailable-decision diagnostic, as tests/character-evaluator.test.ts asserts for the Devil purchased traits after an ancestry switch. The clean outcomes below therefore assume the wizard's prune step clears the stale selection first; the tests must exercise both paths, the pruned one and the stale-selection diagnostic.
removalExpectations.dropNimblestep: Its readable entitlement disappears; no unconditional field moves.
removalExpectations.dropPolderGeist: Its conditionalEffects entry disappears; ordinary speed is unchanged, because it never contributed there.
removalExpectations.dropReactiveTumble: Its readable triggered-action content disappears; no unconditional field moves.
removalExpectations.changeAncestryToDevil: Only Devil and Polder have content modules today, so Devil is the only concrete target: size becomes 1M because the Devil contribution sets it, Shadowmeld and Small! are removed, every purchased Polder trait and its effects are removed, and Devil's own contributions apply. Any other ancestry yields unsupported-option and no ancestry baseline. Class, career, culture, array and authored details are preserved.
removalExpectations.swapTraitWithinBudget: The removed trait's every effect disappears in the same evaluation that adds the new one. Provenance is recomputed from selections on every evaluation, so assert on derived values and readable content rather than on provenance residue, which cannot fail.
